match.reason: Neither bank point teaches gathering facts from reliable sources, organising them under headings, or citing where information came from; discursive writing and critical writing are different ideas.

draft.title: Writing from research
card: Informative writing explains a topic using facts. The facts come from research, not from the writer's opinion.
Choose reliable sources. These are usually written by experts or trusted organisations, such as a university, a government agency or a museum, and can be checked against other sources.
Organise the facts so readers can follow them. Use clear headings, or give each paragraph a topic sentence that names its one main idea.
Say where information came from. Naming the source, in the text or in a reference list, lets readers check the facts and shows the writer did not make them up.
draft.remember: Use reliable sources, group the facts under clear headings, and name where each fact came from.

a.q: Why should an informative text name the source of its facts?
opts: So readers can check the facts and trust the writer
So the text can be made longer with more detail
So the writer can show which opinion is correct
So the headings can be left out of the text
a.why: Naming sources lets readers check the information and shows it was gathered honestly. It does not exist to add length or to push an opinion, and headings are a separate way to organise the text.
a.clue: Think about what a reader can do once they know the source.

b.q: Liam is writing a report on how coral reefs are protected. Which source should he trust most for facts?
opts: A report from a marine science research institute
A comment left under a holiday video online
A post by a friend who once went snorkelling
An advertisement for a reef tour company
b.why: A research institute is made up of experts and its work can be checked. The other sources are based on opinion, a single experience or an aim to sell tours, so they are less reliable for facts.
b.clue: Which source is written by experts who study the topic?

a.best: So readers can check the facts and trust the writer

b.best: A report from a marine science research institute
